name: Hogweed
grown_as: A native wild flower of hedgerows, verges and rough grassland, very popular with insects. Biennial or short-lived perennial. Its sap can cause skin burns in sunlight.
habit: A coarse upright plant 1 to 2 m with a thick, ridged, hollow stem covered in stiff downward hairs. Large rough leaves at the base and smaller ones up the stem.

leaf.arrangement: Large leaves from the base; alternate up the stem
leaf.type: Compound, once pinnate with 3 to 9 leaflets (often 5)
leaf.leaflets: Large and broad, 10 to 25 cm, each lobed into 3 to 5 broad lobes; the lowest pair on stalks, the upper ones stalkless
leaf.outline: Whole leaf up to 60 cm, oblong
leaf.base: Leaflets rounded or wedge-shaped at the base
leaf.margin: Coarsely and irregularly toothed all round the lobes
leaf.surface: Rough, with stiff hairs on both sides
leaf.stalk: Hairy, with a broad sheath at the base that wraps the stem

flower.form: Large flat-topped compound umbels with a ragged edge
flower.petals: Five per flower, deeply notched; on the outer flowers the outward-facing petals are much larger (up to 10 mm)
flower.centre: Small pale stamens and a greenish swollen base
flower.behind: Few or no bracts; several bristle-like bracteoles
flower.carried: At the top of the stem and branches on stout stalks, facing up; 7 to 25 rays

fruit: Flat round to oval seeds 7 to 10 mm in pairs, pale straw with a thin wing round the edge and 2 to 4 dark club-shaped lines running from the top halfway down each face
seedling: Two narrow oval seed leaves, then first true leaves rounded to kidney-shaped, lobed and hairy
winter: Dead hollow stems with seed umbels stand; some green leaves may remain at the base in a mild winter

leaf: once pinnate with a few large broad lobed leaflets
rough hairy surface and sheathing stalk
bloom: large flat umbel of many rays
outer flowers with much larger notched outer petals
seed: flat round pale seed with a thin wing
dark club-shaped lines from the top
seedling: first true leaf rounded and lobed
young: large rough lobed leaves from the base
dormant: dead hollow stems standing with old umbels

look_alikes: Giant hogweed (Heracleum mantegazzianum) is 2 to 5 m tall with purple-blotched stems, huge sharply cut leaves and umbels to 50 cm; it is dangerous. Wild angelica has a smooth purplish stem, finely toothed leaflets and domed umbels. Cow parsley has fine fern-like leaves.
